text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's cabinet has approved a programme for job protection, unemployment reduction and encouraging employment for young people, the cabinet said.
- Poland expressed interest in buying Russia's S-300 anti-aircraft system, an equivalent of the U.S. Patriot missile system, during a visit to Moscow by deputy defence minister Andrzej Karkoszka.
- Deputy Lidia Bladek has renounced her membership in the Polish Peasants Party (PSL) parliamentary caucus and moved to the opposition centrist Union for Freedom (UW).
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's Consumer and Competition Protection Office (UOKK) will not take action against state-owned telecommunications firm Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) in response to reports of a TPSA connection price increase announced by the Era GSM mobile phone operator. The price rise has not violated the law in any way, UOKK said.
- Poland's cabinet said it would scrap the separately-paid road tax and include it in fuel prices. The change will result in a price increase of up to 0.12 zloty per litre.
- Daewoo-FSO car maker will apply to Polish banks for development and construction credits totalling $200 million, the company said.

- The Heros SA non-life insurance firm earned a net profit of 435,000 zlotys in 1996, which will fuel the firm's reserve capital, the company's general shareholders meeting decided. Its sister company, Heros Life SA, made a net loss of 4.793 million zlotys in the period. The loss will be covered by Heros' profits in the next few years.
- Airbus Industries aviation consortium will contract 200 components for the A319 A320 and A321 aircraft to be made by the PZL Swidnik and PZL Mielec aircraft maker.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- The annual sales of the Novell netware maker in Poland have reached $15 million, the company estimated.
- General Motors Poland plans to continue assembling the Opel Astra model at the Warsaw Zeran plant using Hungarian-made bodies, the company said.
- The Naleczowianka mineral water plant has launched a new bottling line, the output capacity of which is 10,000 bottles per hour. The new facility cost $7.3 million to build.
- The U.S. McDonald's fast food chain is now operating 74 outlets in 33 cities around Poland. The chain has invested $73 million in development in the last five years.
- The Soft-tronik Polska Wroclaw software firm has changed into a joint stock company and plans to apply for a listing this year, marketing and services director Zbigniew Siama said.

- The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) will probably accept the share issue prospectus produced by KGHM Polska Miedz copper conglomerate at the KPW meeting tomorrow. KGHM expects a share listing in Warsaw and London at the beginning of July.
ZYCIE

- The Lukbut footwear maker, co-owned by the Third National Investment Fund (NFI) No 3, will present the KPW with a share issue prospectus. Lukbut wants to list its shares on the Warsaw bourse's parallel market.
PARKIET
- The listed BFK cable maker will soon receive the SABS product quality certificate which will allow BFK to enter the South African market, BFK said.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
